# Outer contacts: actual cap selectors and a valid perspective localization

This note concerns an ACTUAL single cap group of the new H-tied separator, not a source-plane compression of an arbitrary old separator. It verifies the cap-selection issue in the contributor's outer-envelope proposal and gives additional legitimate convex tests on nonsmooth contact faces.

Assume the full-rank deepest-source face has an affine homothetic envelope

    T_z=y(z)+ell(z)D,  ell(z)>0, K_z subset T_z,

where y and ell are affine on the full base affine hull, D is a d-dimensional convex body with 0 in its interior, and source fibers on the occupied face equal T_z. All the group's critical caps have the common pointed form

    margin_i(z,y(z)+ell(z)xi)=ell(z)[u_i.xi+b_i].         (1)

Each cap is proper on D. For the actual H group, b_i=epsilon f_D Gamma(u_i)>0. The full-rank quantile propagation proving (1) requires a menu based at an interior witness of the relevant deepest hull. A cap merely active at a boundary source does not automatically have this property.

In the explicitly constructed H separator, if the positive-contact hull has full base rank and a relative-interior integer point, then the hull of ALL deepest bases also has such a point. Its only maximal occupied face is the full hull, so that construction has ONE group anchored at an interior witness. Formula (1) then applies to every positive cap of this same separator. This is a property of the chosen physical cover, not of a parameter-only reduction.

## 1. Supporting allocations disappear on these particular outer contacts

For unit outer normal n define the affine envelope gap

    g_n(z,x)=n.y(z)+ell(z)h_D(n)-n.x >=0 on C.

Let E be the actual normal-bundle outer contact {g_n=0}. At such a point xi=(x-y(z))/ell(z) lies in partial D, indeed in its exposed face F_D(n).

If a hyperplane cuts the interior of a full-dimensional convex D, its intersection with partial D has H_(d-1) measure zero. One direct proof is to consider its full-dimensional section in that hyperplane: every relative-interior section point is interior to D, since an ambient support normal at it would have to vanish on the section plane and would contradict the proper crossing. Thus the boundary intersection is contained in the relative boundary of the section, which is H_(d-1)-null. For d=1 a proper cutting point is not either endpoint.

Apply this to every proper cap plane {u_i.xi+b_i=0}. In each sampled fiber, physical outer contact is contained in the homothetic image of partial D. Its intersection with the cap plane is therefore surface-null. There are finitely many fibers and caps. Consequently the SAME actual boundary selector W, with all its inside/outside allocations retained elsewhere, satisfies on E almost everywhere

    W(z,x)=w(xi),    w(xi)=sum_i omega_i 1_{u_i.xi+b_i>=0}.  (2)

Any alternative values on the null planes give the same measure. In particular fractional supporting selections cannot alter (2). This conclusion does not require strict convexity of D.

## 2. Normal-localized outer-contact stress

Let Phi_t(n,z,x)=psi(n) exp(-t g_n(z,x)), where psi is nonnegative continuous. This is a continuous normal-dependent globally convex physical field: g_n is affine in (z,x). It is therefore in the actual H cone. Since g_n>=0 on C, dominated convergence as t increases gives the legitimate contact restriction

    integral_E psi(n) Xi(z,x) dS <=0.                  (3)

The bounded H response has Xi=W-beta+R_epsilon with |R_epsilon|<=C epsilon uniformly on the compact proper-source class. Thus (3) gives the corresponding normal-conditional inequality for the actual outer-contact measure. It does not allow conditioning further on an arbitrary subset of a positive-dimensional face F_D(n).

If D is strictly convex, each F_D(n) is a single point xi(n). Then w(xi(n)) is constant at fixed n across all sampled outer contacts. The own source fiber supplies a positive homothetic copy of the entire surface-area measure of D inside the contact measure. Consequently (3) implies

    w(xi(n))<=beta+C epsilon   for S_D-almost every n.  (4)

This is the precise reason strict convexity simplifies this step; the cap-selector issue itself was already settled by (2).

## 3. The correct extra tests on a nonsmooth face

For any nonnegative finite convex function phi on R^d define, on the positive affine domain ell>0,

    F(z,x)=ell(z) phi((x-y(z))/ell(z)).                  (5)

It is the usual convex perspective composed with affine functions, hence convex. On a fixed compact neighborhood of C, ell has a positive floor. A globally finite convex extension sufficient for the physical cone can be obtained by taking a supremum of bounded affine supports of this perspective on a slightly larger compact neighborhood; local Lipschitz continuity gives bounded support coefficients and equality on C. Equivalently, for a finite maximum of affine phi, (5) is already a finite maximum of globally affine functions.

Use

    [F(z,x)-t g_n(z,x)]_+                               (6)

as the convex physical field, with any nonnegative continuous normal multiplier. Let t increase. On C it decreases to F 1_E and is bounded by F_+, so dominated convergence gives

    integral_E ell(z) phi(xi) Xi(z,x) dS <=0.           (7)

Finite piecewise-affine convex tests suffice; standard compact approximation extends to all finite convex phi. Thus a nonsmooth exposed face retains an actual convex-test inequality in its pointed coordinates. It is not legitimate to replace this law by a centroid or by uniform intrinsic face volume without proof.

For a fixed facet normal, if E_z denotes the corresponding pointed contact subset of F_D(n), the density in (7) relative to pointed H_(d-1) is weighted by

    sum_z ell(z)^d 1_(E_z)(xi).

The extra ell compared with ordinary surface scaling comes from the perspective. These actual contact sets and weights remain part of the measure; they are not an arbitrary source-label conditioning.

## 4. Own projective cap credit in the strictly convex subcase

Let P_D(xi)=1+a_D.xi be the actual energy normalizer of (D,0), and put

    q_D(xi)=xi.n/P_D(xi)^d=h_D(n)/P_D(xi)^d.

It is a positive surface density. The projective image xi -> xi/P_D(xi) is convex and has centroid zero by the energy first-moment equation. Its Jacobian is P_D^(-d-1). The divergence identity

    div(xi/P_D(xi)^d)=d/P_D(xi)^(d+1)

shows that, on every through-zero cone, q_D surface mass equals d times projective-image volume. Hence every pointed cap containing zero has q_D mass at least Gamma_d of the total: first use its parallel through-zero halfspace, then ordinary centroid Grunbaum in the projective image.

Each cap in (1) contains zero, and sum_i omega_i=1 for the actual single group. Thus

    integral w q_D dS_D >= Gamma_d integral q_D dS_D.    (8)

There is an exact bound in the actual H response: all own-energy, own-volume and covariance contributions are nonnegative, so Xi>=W-B_star with B_star=beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM). Repeating (3)--(4) with B_star gives

    beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM)>=Gamma_d.                     (9)

This implies beta>=Gamma_d-C epsilon whenever D is strictly convex and the stated single-group full-rank envelope hypotheses hold. This is a valid restricted consequence. At nonsmooth faces, (7) is the surviving interface; the needed comparison for its aggregate contact density is not proved here. Nor does this note claim that the general attained source hull satisfies the single-group/full-rank hypotheses.
